title: The False Card
verdict: Theo Pierce was responsible for the disappearance of a first-edition map plate.
intent: Theo Pierce wanted to sell the map plate to cover an undisclosed debt.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the rare-room librarian controlled the tour bell and handled the atlas last.
Remove a first-edition map plate from its checked location.
Hide the item in a conservation folder labeled as tissue scraps.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a first-edition map plate disappeared from a public library rare-book room during a school tour.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the tour bell rang two minutes early.
The physical trace was fresh paper lint on the atlas cradle.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a bone folder with paper dust along one side.
The item could be concealed in a conservation folder labeled as tissue scraps.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the rare-room librarian knew the atlas cradle had a loose back rail.
The access pattern mattered because the rare-room librarian controlled the tour bell and handled the atlas last.
The motive was to sell the map plate to cover an undisclosed debt.
distractor_cues: a patron asking many questions about old maps
a student aide left alone near the desk
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
